outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
nodes.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

nodes.question: Do the main giraffe subjects remain substantially photographically rendered beneath a surface treatment, constituting an unmet part of turning the image into a chalk drawing?
nodes.criteria: Inspect the giraffes' contours, markings, shading and surfaces directly. Pass only if their rendering clearly remains photographic rather than chalk-drawn, so the requested transformation is demonstrably incomplete in the main subjects. Texture, blur or grain alone cannot establish this defect. Recognizable spots, realistic proportions and detailed shading can occur in chalk drawings and do not independently establish photographic residue. Fail if this specific obstacle is visibly absent because the subjects read as chalk-rendered. Unknown if photographic rendering cannot reliably be distinguished from detailed chalk drawing. Failure establishes only the absence of this obstacle, not completion of the whole image.
nodes.binding: O1: Investigate a specific potentially unmet part of R1, namely the medium-like rendering of the main subjects. This check adds no requirement for a particular chalk technique, background, or loss of recognizable detail.

nodes.question: Does comparison with the input image show that the requested chalk-drawing transformation has progressed?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comparison shows some change toward rendering the image as a chalk drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete. Fail if there is no requested progress; unrelated edits alone do not count. Unknown if the images or comparison are insufficient to determine progress.
nodes.binding: O1 and the rubric: assess progress toward the requested chalk-drawing transformation, not unrelated edits.

nodes.question: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
nodes.criteria: Apply the original instruction and rubric. Use only valid observed evidence. Return complete (yes) when s1 passes and s_subject_medium does not validly pass: the independent whole-image endpoint establishes completion, while a targeted fail establishes only absence of that obstacle and a targeted unknown adds no contrary fact. If s1 and s_subject_medium both pass, return unknown because the endpoint and specific incompleteness evidence conflict; do not resolve that conflict using progress alone. Otherwise, established incompleteness means either s1 explicitly fails or s_subject_medium validly passes. With established incompleteness, return partial when s2 passes and absent (no) when s2 fails. Return unknown if incompleteness is not established and s1 does not validly pass, even when s2 reports progress. Return unknown when the progress evidence needed for partial or absent is unresolved. Unknown, invalid or skipped observations are not failures. A skipped targeted check supplies no obstacle evidence; a skipped progress check cannot establish progress or its absence. Unrelated edits never count as requested progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

It can return unknown despite known progress when the whole-image endpoint is unknown and the targeted incompleteness check does not pass; the rubric instead calls for partial when some requested progress is established without complete fulfillment. It also treats a pass on the targeted check as established incompleteness, although that check only establishes that the subjects remain photographic, not that no other part of the requested transformation is complete.
parsed.source_clause: partial means some progress without complete fulfillment.
parsed.counterexample: Suppose s1 is unknown, s_subject_medium passes, and s2 passes. The saved composition returns partial, which is supported. But if s1 is unknown, s_subject_medium fails, and s2 passes, it returns unknown even though progress is known and completion is not established. Conversely, a targeted pass can establish incompleteness even if the rest of the image is already a chalk drawing, so the program may report partial where the requested end result is complete.
